correctness.rationale: The distinct-output ball is the union of Hamming radius-one neighborhoods of every one-deletion descendant; codebooks are exactly cliques of the graph with an edge iff intersection cardinality <5. Inspected the actual verify.py and its complete bit-set maximum-clique branch-and-bound proof: independent sets in its greedy coloring give a safe upper bound for each remaining branch; every compatible extension is considered. Reimplemented channel-ball construction and full exact maximum-clique search independently for all lengths 3..9: maxima (8,5,5,6,8,12,16), edges (28,38,115,552,2917,15194,75483), and at n=9 exactly 416465 recursive calls. Verified the seven lower-bound witnesses logically against the same channel model. This is a complete finite-domain computation, not an infinite claim. A codeword is padded to exactly n bits; repeated output words are deduplicated.

evidence: Li–Sun–Ge (2026) Theorem 4.6 constructs five-read codes with asymptotic-type redundancy 3 log_2 n+4; it is a lower bound on attainable code size, not an optimum for every n≤9.
Song–Cai–Quek read-intersection bounds apply under additional Hamming-distance conditions and do not certify this entire maximum-clique spectrum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General constructions and constrained distance bounds do not dominate an exact all-codeword finite optimum without a matching universal upper bound; no such implication was identified in inspected relevant material.

evidence: The only directly comparable channel requires five distinct outputs; stronger uniqueness decoding (one-read) implies feasible five-read codes but not their maximum.
Li–Sun–Ge construction supplies code sizes, not the global packing upper bound for short words.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new finite optimum is not numerically or logically implied by reported lower bounds and stronger one-read separation criteria.

evidence: The published one-read binary DS_{1,2}(7)=3, DS_{1,2}(8)=5 classification requires disjoint output balls; here distinct five reads require pairwise overlaps strictly less than five.
Li–Sun–Ge use the same one-deletion/at-most-one-substitution error operation in their five-read reconstruction framework.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The model is a five-distinct-read reconstruction packing: intersection <5, not the one-read channel with intersection zero. Reinterpreting the coding convention does not turn one-read exact capacities into the asserted seven five-read capacities.

value.rationale: The natural finite-blocklength five-read reconstruction capacity is a primary optimization invariant. A complete n=3..9 capacity profile, including a 512-vertex n9 optimum and the counterintuitive decrease 8 to 5 from n3 to n4, is a meaningful benchmark for designs and finite-channel bounds, even without an all-length theorem.

limitations: Binary alphabet; exact one deletion and at most one substitution; distinct output words and five distinct reads; lengths 3 through 9 only. No decoder, asymptotic capacity, uniqueness, formal proof or external attestation.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact five-read small-blocklength table could duplicate some or all entries.
